title: Magnon Polarization Textures and Transport in Antiferromagnets and Altermagnets
abstract: Antiferromagnets (AFMs) host magnons that can exhibit fully circular, elliptic and linear polarizations of sublattice magnetization dynamics. We analyze theoretically different momentum-space magnon polarization textures and magnon transport in collinear AFMs and altermagnets (AMs). The sensitivity of the polarization texture to a magnon momentum direction determines two regimes of magnon polarization kinetics: The Dyakonov-Perel relaxation or its dephasing due to asynchronous Larmor precession. For an easy-axis AFM, magnetic field parallel to the N{é}el vector leads to the suppression of the magnetic dipolar interaction-induced Dyakonov-Perel relaxation, accompanied by the increase in the magnon spin-diffusion length and its counter-intuitive growth with temperature. For a perpendicular orientation, instead, relaxation of circular polarization of magnons is enhanced due to Larmor precession. Finally, extremely anisotropic relaxation of magnon polarization is predicted for AMs or AFMs having Dzyaloshinskii-Morya interaction.
summary: This work provides a theoretical framework for understanding how magnon polarization textures dictate transport in antiferromagnets and altromagnets. By analyzing the interplay between Larmor precession and relaxation mechanisms, the authors predict field-dependent changes in spin-diffusion length and the Hanle effect. This is crucial for designing spintronic devices based on magnetic excitations.
main_problem: The paper theoretically analyzes the magnon polarization textures and subsequent transport mechanisms in antiferromagnets (AFMs) and altromagnets (AMs).
main_result: It demonstrates that the magnon polarization kinetics are governed by two regimes—Dyakonov-Perel relaxation or dephasing due to Larmor precession—and predicts that external fields can suppress relaxation, leading to enhanced spin-diffusion lengths.
method: The analysis employs theoretical tools including the Holstein-Primakoff transformation, Bogoliubov diagonalization, and Boltzmann kinetic theory applied to the magnon density matrix.
model_or_system: The study focuses on collinear AFMs and AMs, modeled using a general magnetic Hamiltonian incorporating exchange, anisotropy, Zeeman, DM, and dipolar interactions. The dynamics are tracked via a pseudospin density matrix.
key_observables: Magnon polarization textures ($\vec{\sigma}_k$), magnon spin-diffusion length, and the Hanle effect signature (suppression of $S_z$ vs. $B_0$).
important_parameters: The relative strengths of relaxation mechanisms (e.g., $	au_g^{-1}$ vs. $\Gamma_z$), and the external magnetic field $B_0$ relative to characteristic relaxation times.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the small canting angle approximation ($	heta_0 \ll 1$) and the semiclassical approximation for the density matrix.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Bloch sphere for the magnon pseudospin, the momentum-dependent Larmor frequency vectors ($\vec{\Omega}_k$), and the dependence of ellipticity ($\Theta$) on distance and field.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the effective magnon Hamiltonian and polarization dynamics to analyzing the kinetic equation for the pseudospin, culminating in the detailed discussion of the Hanle effect and the role of anisotropic DP relaxation.
why_interesting: The detailed treatment of magnon polarization dynamics and the connection to relaxation mechanisms like DP relaxation provides a rich framework for understanding spin transport in magnetic insulators, which shares conceptual overlap with open quantum systems dynamics.
